title: Cymba schematic cerebral nerve fibres and projected vagus pathways — reference v8
direction: Detailed exaggerated violet central neural arbors replace broad brain glow. Networks project onto opaque marble over the upper cranium, separate from the localized upper-ear target and dashed deep neck route.
caption: Schematic brain network and projected vagus pathways.
notes: Cerebral motifs are enlarged artistic neuronal representations, not an anatomical fibre-tract map, measured activation or evidence of device efficacy.
These central brain-network symbols are distinct from the vagus nerve. They are not drawn as peripheral vagus branches across the scalp.
Ear target and dashed deep cervical routes remain approximate schematics; ear and neck pathways are hidden in the rear view.
Head remains solid stone with no cutaway or glass. No live-site code or 3D model was changed.
Generated views may differ in geometry or pathway placement; reconcile during 3D modelling.

prompts.stage: replace diffuse brain glow with neural fibres
prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: supplied solid ivory marble mannequin with purple ear stimulation, dashed neck pathway and broad purple glow on the upper head.

CHANGE ONLY THE BRAIN-ACTIVITY VISUAL:
Remove the broad purple wash, blurry patches and soft spotlight-like glow from the upper head. Replace them with CLEARLY VISIBLE, FINELY BRANCHING NEURAL FIBRES that look like stimulated neuronal connections in the brain. The user explicitly wants nerves, not a diffuse glow.

Show this as a luminous illustration of CENTRAL BRAIN NETWORKS projected onto the opaque stone over the upper cranial region. Fine violet nerve fibres should form several distinct organic dendritic arbors, with delicate tapering branches, small interconnections, naturally curved fibre bundles and a few short lavender-white segments suggesting signals travelling through them. Biological neural fibres, not electrical circuitry, lightning cracks, vessels, tree roots or a mesh grid. More detailed and visibly active than a few simple arcs, but still refined and readable. Keep plenty of clear ivory stone between groups. No solid color wash behind the fibres.

The central brain network is INDEPENDENT of the ear and neck vagus route. Do NOT grow a single nerve tree from the ear into the scalp. Do NOT connect the ear highlight, cheek, neck line or any lower-head point to the cortical fibres. Keep a clean visible gap of plain stone around the ear and temple below the central network. This is a schematic surface projection of neurons inside the brain, not a claim that the vagus branches across the scalp. Neural arbors spread mainly across the upper lateral cranium and crown, following the brain region in silhouette. Use several smaller interconnected arbors across that region rather than one giant central trunk.

PURPLE dominates: electric violet, amethyst and lilac with crisp luminous filament cores and only narrow soft bloom. Avoid hot-pink dominance. Fibres immediately legible at normal image size. No huge glowing dots or large neuron balls.

PRESERVE ALL ELSE EXACTLY:
Same beautiful ivory marble sculpture, subtle veining, solid closed opaque skull, blank open stone eyes, facial identity and neutral expression, anatomically complete ear, small localized cymba-conchae violet fibre target, single dashed anterolateral neck projection, base, camera angle, lighting and pale grey studio background. Keep the corrected ear/neck route unchanged. No cutaway, glass, transparency, visible interior anatomy or raised brain folds. No text, labels, logo, earbuds, cables or extra objects.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: four-angle 3D sculpture reference with schematic brain network.
Reference image: exact sculpture and neural treatment to preserve.

Create a square 2x2 reference sheet of the same sculpture, front, left profile, right profile and rear. Front at top left, profile looking right top right, profile looking left bottom left, rear bottom right. Equal scale and eye-level orthographic cameras, same neutral upright head relative to neck, complete crown and neck base, consistent aligned bases and margins.
Preserve reference's exact face, blank open carved-stone eyes with no iris/pupil, quiet expression, honed ivory marble with faint veins, whole solid closed head and neck. No glass, cutaway, transparent head or internal organs.

Central brain-network visualization: reproduce the reference's detailed violet branching neuronal arbors, with tapered dendritic filaments, small irregular interconnections and a few short bright impulse segments. These are exaggerated schematic projections of cerebral neural networks onto the stone over the upper cranium and crown. Keep several discrete neural clusters, with white stone between them, clearly readable nerve fibres instead of a broad glow. Follow the same 3D placement as the camera moves, including continuing onto upper posterior cranium. No diffuse purple color wash behind them. No circuits, lightning cracks, blood vessels or metallic wires. Purple/amethyst dominant, fine lavender-white cores.

Do not connect these central brain-network clusters to the peripheral vagus marks. Keep a clear plain-stone gap around the ear and temple below the cerebral network. No single giant nerve tree growing from ear into scalp.

Peripheral vagus marks match reference: bright LOCAL nerve-ending cluster in CYMBA CONCHAE, the upper conchal pocket above crus of helix; no ear canal/lobe/whole-ear highlight. A separate vivid dashed violet line projects the deep cervical course on the ANTEROLATERAL side of the neck under jaw angle alongside the throat. One route per side only, no branching neck mesh. Front can show both neck routes; each profile shows its near-side route. Do not add a cheek arc or expose a cable between ear and neck.

REAR VIEW: show the cerebral network on upper head, but BOTH EARS and the ENTIRE LOWER NAPE AND NECK are PLAIN IVORY STONE. The ear's anterior cymba target and anterolateral deep neck paths are occluded from this rear direction. No purple marks behind ears, no rear-neck dashes or nerves. Never relocate pathways to make them visible.

Clean cool pale grey studio background, soft lighting, contact shadows, all views sharply focused. No earbuds, cables, jewelry, hair, clothing or added torso.
Below the four panels in a small clean charcoal sans-serif caption write exactly: "Schematic brain network and projected vagus pathways."
No other text, logos, watermark or labels.
